scope: Original explanatory crosswalk and synthetic boundary subsets; not certification, full requirement verification, or an official OWASP mapping.

C9.2.1.summary: Verify trusted human approval before privileged or hard-to-reverse effects.

C9.2.2.summary: Present complete canonical action parameters to reviewers.

C9.2.3.summary: Assign reversibility classes from trusted action definitions.

C9.2.4.summary: Enforce the action class at the execution boundary.

C9.2.5.summary: Bound changes to prompts, tools, and runtime configuration.

C9.2.6.summary: Supplement deterministic gates with a model-based high-risk action review.

C9.2.7.summary: Protect the model-based review from adversarial manipulation and bypass.

C9.2.8.summary: Bind approvals cryptographically to parameters, identity, context, and a one-use nonce.

C9.2.9.summary: Keep approval issuer credentials outside the agent runtime.

C9.2.10.summary: Gate every chain at its highest-impact reversibility class.

entries.name: Agent Goal Hijacking

mappings.rationale: An external effect cannot change the fixed trusted goal through retrieved instructions.
Retrieved data cannot rewrite the boundary's instruction policy.

entries.limitations: One fixed-goal boundary; no semantic prompt-injection classifier or full action-review workflow.

entries.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation

mappings.rationale: The tool catalog supplies the effect class rather than accepting a caller label.
Unknown effectful tools have no authorized execution path.

entries.limitations: One synthetic tool catalog; no real tool sandbox or argument-complete domain policy.

entries.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse

mappings.rationale: A signed child grant binds requester, context, nonce, and narrower action scope.

entries.limitations: Grant-binding subset of approval context; no human authentication or distributed delegation service.

entries.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities

mappings.rationale: A pinned manifest cannot acquire extra tools after registration.

entries.limitations: Synthetic manifest integrity, not package signing, dependency verification, or a complete supply-chain defense.

entries.name: Unexpected Code Execution

mappings.rationale: Only the narrow non-effectful expression class is admitted before a synthetic code-result write.

entries.limitations: A small AST verifier, not unrestricted code execution or a general-purpose sandbox.

entries.name: Memory and Context Poisoning

mappings.rationale: Untrusted episodic content cannot become privileged persistent instruction state.

entries.limitations: Signed provenance admission subset; TTL and contradiction handling are in the separate ASI05/ASI06 sample.

entries.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication

mappings.rationale: The peer handoff authenticates final identity, target, parameters, context, and nonce before effect formation.

entries.limitations: Authenticated handoff-binding subset, not an encrypted transport or non-repudiation service.

entries.name: Cascading Failures

mappings.rationale: The registered chain has trusted per-step reversibility classes.
Budget and chain-class mismatches stop the accepting boundary.
A read prefix cannot lower approval below the maximum class in the chain.

entries.limitations: One chain admission boundary; retry damping and concurrent swarm budgets are in the separate ASI08/ASI10 sample.

entries.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation

mappings.rationale: A trusted fixture reviewer issues the required approval before the effect.
Approval evidence covers the complete canonical parameter object without truncation.
Parameter mutation, identity/context drift, and approval nonce replay fail at commit.

entries.limitations: A trusted reviewer stub, not reviewer authentication, UI safety verification, or isolated issuer keys.

entries.name: Rogue Agents

mappings.rationale: A previously approved high-impact effect is blocked when current authority is revoked.
Containment limits the consequences of rogue self-modification; this fixture does not detect intent or prove all self-modification controls.

entries.limitations: Live revocation at a single boundary; signed swarm kill and behavioral monitoring are in the separate ASI08/ASI10 sample.
